utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: We will now have today's invocation delivered by Reverend Philip Jackson, Rector of Trinity Church Wall Street.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Welcome, Reverend Jackson.

chapters.summary: Reverend Jackson thanks the Council, notes Trinity Church's 329-year history, and prays for guidance, humility, and compassion for vulnerable New Yorkers.
chapters.title: Reverend Phillip Jackson delivers invocation

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Reverend Phillip Jackson
utterances.text: I would like to begin by thanking all the members of the council, those who invited me, and all of you for the work that you do.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Reverend Phillip Jackson
utterances.text: My name is Phil Jackson.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Reverend Phillip Jackson
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Reverend Phillip Jackson
utterances.text: I'm the rector of Trinity Church.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Reverend Phillip Jackson
utterances.text: Trinity Church, of course, has been a part of this neighborhood for 329 years.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Reverend Phillip Jackson
utterances.text: And it's the first time that I've been invited to be here, and I'm honored to be here.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Reverend Phillip Jackson
utterances.text: So I invite you all to join me in prayer as you begin today's session.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Reverend Phillip Jackson
utterances.text: Let us pray.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Reverend Phillip Jackson
utterances.text: God, our creator, we thank you for bringing us here today in service of the people of our great city.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Reverend Phillip Jackson
utterances.text: We thank you for this day and for this work.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Reverend Phillip Jackson
utterances.text: We pray that you will guide our council members and be present in their collective wisdom as they work to serve our neighbors.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Reverend Phillip Jackson
utterances.text: Bring them together in a spirit of humility, integrity, and openness as they consider the issues that affect those who live and work in this diverse, ever-evolving city

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Reverend Phillip Jackson
utterances.text: that we all call home.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Reverend Phillip Jackson
utterances.text: Be with them in their deliberations and decisions.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Reverend Phillip Jackson
utterances.text: And we keep in our hearts those who are homeless, unemployed, sick or hungry, and all who experience any need or want.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Reverend Phillip Jackson
utterances.text: We remember in our prayers those who are here in search of safety and a better life for themselves and their families.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Reverend Phillip Jackson
utterances.text: We pray that they may encounter kindness and compassion on their journey.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Reverend Phillip Jackson
utterances.text: We give thanks for all who work tirelessly on behalf of our neighbors.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Reverend Phillip Jackson
utterances.text: Give them strength to continue their important work, and courage and hope to sustain them when they are discouraged.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Reverend Phillip Jackson
utterances.text: We thank our council members for the gift of their service to their constituents and to one another.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Reverend Phillip Jackson
utterances.text: May they be.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Reverend Phillip Jackson
utterances.text: faithful representatives of their neighborhoods, while serving also the good of our entire city.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Reverend Phillip Jackson
utterances.text: We ask your blessing upon them and upon this meeting that their labor may be fruitful and their decisions wise.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Reverend Phillip Jackson
utterances.text: In your name we pray.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Reverend Phillip Jackson
utterances.text: Amen.

chapters.summary: Council Member Marte recounts Reverend Jackson's career and service at Trinity Church, thanks him for his community work, and moves unanimous consent to spread the invocation.
chapters.title: Council Member Marte honors Reverend Phillip Jackson and moves to spread invocation

utterances.speaker: Christopher Marte
utterances.text: Thank you, Majority Leader.

utterances.speaker: Christopher Marte
utterances.text: The Reverend Philip A.

utterances.speaker: Christopher Marte
utterances.text: Jackson was named the 19th Rector of Trinity Church in February 2022.

utterances.speaker: Christopher Marte
utterances.text: In this role, he serves as the spiritual leader of the parish, while also managing operation, parish programs, the clergy, staff, and all resources and facilities of the church.

utterances.speaker: Christopher Marte
utterances.text: Prior to his institution as rector, Father Jackson served as priest in charge for two years.

utterances.speaker: Christopher Marte
utterances.text: Father Jackson has focused Trinity's energy and resources on four main areas, offering meaningful and beautiful worship services and opportunities to build Christian community, providing programming and support through grants and other activities for children and youth,

utterances.speaker: Christopher Marte
utterances.text: supporting New York City through outreach, grants, advocacy, and the work with local partners, and strengthening our ties with the Anglican Communion and the Episcopal Church.

utterances.speaker: Christopher Marte
utterances.text: Father Jackson joined Trinity Church in 2015, leading the congregation's life as a parish through ministry.

utterances.speaker: Christopher Marte
utterances.text: programs including liturgies, music, education, programming, membership, and stewardship.

utterances.speaker: Christopher Marte
utterances.text: Before coming to Trinity, Jackson was director at Christ Church at the Ascension in Paradise Valley, Arizona.

utterances.speaker: Christopher Marte
utterances.text: Ordained in 1994, he also served in parishes in Houston and Detroit.

utterances.speaker: Christopher Marte
utterances.text: And was also an attorney in Honolulu.

utterances.speaker: Christopher Marte
utterances.text: I personally want to thank Father Jackson for all his work.

utterances.speaker: Christopher Marte
utterances.text: Lorman Hank could be a really noisy, chaotic place where he brings a calm foundation to Trinity Church.

utterances.speaker: Christopher Marte
utterances.text: And for many years, Trinity Church thought about everywhere else in the world.

utterances.speaker: Christopher Marte
utterances.text: Under his leadership,

utterances.speaker: Christopher Marte
utterances.text: He continues to think about Lower Manhattan, their backyard, and serving some of our old neighbors and new neighbors, no matter where they come from.

utterances.speaker: Christopher Marte
utterances.text: And I want to thank, from all the families that you have helped since I've been in office, from the bottom of our hearts, thank you to you, to your leadership, your vision, and to Trinity Church.

utterances.speaker: Christopher Marte
utterances.text: I make the motion of unanimous consent to spread the invocation and fall upon the record.

utterances.text: It was truly monumental to usher in a new chapter of safety, security, and most importantly, humanity in the story of our city.

utterances.text: But as much as the welfare of our animals and the health of our residents, we also sought to protect the livelihoods of the dedicated workers.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: This legislation sets out a path that the administration has already started moving towards to ensure the industry can wind down and its workers can successfully transition out of it.

chapters.summary: Speaker Menin discusses a Council investigation finding 40% of shops near schools sold prohibited flavored e-cigarettes, and calls for DCWP authority to close repeat violators.
chapters.title: Speaker Menin exposes illegal flavored e-cigarette sales near schools

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Yesterday represented a landmark too as we released a report exposing the widespread availability of flavored e-cigarettes and vapes.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Products that, let's be clear, are already illegal to sell thanks to a bill that the City Council passed in 2019.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Since March, the Council's Oversight and Investigations Division, and I really want to thank them for their amazing work,

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: has gone into 193 businesses located within 500 feet of a public middle or high school across the five boroughs.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Our investigation found that 40% of shops surveyed that carried e-cigarettes offered products with a prohibited flavor, and nearly a third of the schools surveyed had shops with prohibited advertising within 500 feet.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Currently, the Department of Consumer and Worker Protection does not have the authority to close a business solely for...

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: for unlicensed or flavored e-cigarette sales.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Instead, they can issue a simple slap on the wrist in the form of a fine.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Tomorrow, however, we will hear a bill sponsored by Councilmember Mercedes Narcisse to give DCWP the authority to close a business if they have three violations of selling e-cigarettes.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: And we'll continue to look for ways that strengthen enforcement of advertising restrictions near schools.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Vapes are a risk to the health of our children, and let's be clear about that.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: These flavored e-cigarettes are marketed with flavors, bubblegum flavor, candy cane flavor, and packaging marketed to our kids who have developing lungs.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: And we all know there is an explosive rise of cancer among young people here in the city.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: So this is an important public health issue.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: It's our responsibility to deliver on our vision of a safer, healthier city for every New Yorker who calls it home.

chapters.summary: Speaker Menin notes $2.28 billion in pupil transportation contracts, many renewed since the 1970s, and commits to transparency and better service, especially for special needs students.
chapters.title: Speaker Menin questions DOE school busing costs and service

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: As part of the council's oversight role, we also held a hearing to ask about the cost and the performance of the Department of Education's school busing operations.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Pupil transportation is DOE's third largest contract category at $2.28 billion in fiscal 2027, and more taxpayer dollars are being spent than ever before.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: As part of our contract review of the contracts we had requested from DOE, I just want to be clear.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Many of these bus contracts literally go back to the 1970s and then are just renewed each year.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Yet this growth has not led to improved service, and New Yorkers are not experiencing any additional benefit, and we all know this is having a disproportionate effect, particularly on our special needs students.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: We are committed to transparency about how a third of our budget is spent and to make sure the next contracts that DOE selects deliver the services New Yorkers are paying for.

chapters.summary: Speaker Menin wishes everyone a happy Thanksgiving, highlights Small Business Saturday, and notes nearly 200,000 small businesses employ 1 million New Yorkers.
chapters.title: Speaker Menin wishes Thanksgiving and promotes Small Business Saturday

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Looking to next week, I want to wish everyone an early but a very happy Thanksgiving, hoping you have a wonderful time spent with loved ones.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: I'm incredibly thankful to all of you as colleagues and as friends for the hard work that you and all of your teams do every single day to serve our constituents and all New Yorkers.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: And on a personal note, very excited about the Thanksgiving Day Parade.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: I hope many of you will end up being able to go and to join, bring family and loved ones and friends.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: The Saturday after Thanksgiving is Small Business Saturday, and let's be honest, it's wonderful that New York is home to almost 200,000

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: small businesses that employ nearly 1 million New Yorkers, truly forming the backbone of our great city.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: As a former small business owner myself, I know firsthand that every customer is crucial to these institutions, whether you're getting a meal at a restaurant, buying something at a clothing store.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: store or finding your favorite book at a bookstore.

chapters.summary: Speaker Menin wishes a belated happy birthday to Council Member Kevin Riley and an early happy birthday to Council Member Eric Dinowitz.
chapters.title: Speaker Menin recognizes birthdays of Council Members Riley and Dinowitz

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Please join me in wishing a belated happy birthday to Councilmember Kevin Riley.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Who celebrated on the 16th.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: And a happy early birthday to Councilmember Eric Dinowitz, whose birthday is on the 21st.

chapters.summary: Speaker Menin acknowledges Bill Ritter and his WABC colleagues, thanks Council Member Brewer, and praises Ritter's reporting and pursuit of truth.
chapters.title: Speaker Menin honors Bill Ritter for four decades of service

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: So I also want to acknowledge a New York City legend and icon, Bill Ritter, and his wife, Kathleen, and all of his WABC colleagues who have made it here.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: We were so thrilled, and I know many of you were here to join us, to present a proclamation to recognize his four decades of service.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: And thank you to Councilmember Brewer.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: I know how important this was to you.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Bill, we thank you so much for the years and years and years of incredible reporting you've given to our city, to the world of journalism, and most importantly, to the pursuit of truth.

chapters.summary: Speaker Menin welcomes foster youth hosted by Council Member Althea Stevens, saying their lived experiences will help build a better foster care system.
chapters.title: Speaker Menin welcomes Fostering Youth Success Alliance

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: And then finally, I want to welcome a very special group here, hosted by Council Member Althea Stevens, Fostering Youth Success Alliance.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: These young people who've all lived in foster care are spending the day here learning how government works and how their own lived experiences can shape our public policy.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: While we hope that they all learn a great deal, we honestly are learning more from them because we know that their experiences are going to help us build a better foster care system that truly...

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: will meet the needs of our young people.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: So thank you for being here.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Thank you for using your voices and for helping us build a city where every young person has the opportunity and the support to thrive.

chapters.summary: Speaker Menin extends congratulations to Brooklyn's Hakeem Jeffries on his nomination to be Speaker of the House of Representatives.
chapters.title: Speaker Menin congratulates Hakeem Jeffries on Speaker nomination

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: And now, before I get on to our stated agenda, I lastly...

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Want to extend an amazing congratulations to Brooklyn's own Hakeem Jeffries on being nominated to be Speaker of the House of Representatives.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: This is a great source of pride for us here in New York, and we so look forward to continuing this incredible partnership between the City Council and the House.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: So we want to extend our deepest congratulations.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin

utterances.text: Pre-considered resolutions sponsored by Councilmember Linda Lee granting an Article 11 property tax exemption for Ford and Bedford Cluster Phase 3 in the districts of Councilmember Periana Sanchez and Oswald Piles.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Today, we'll also vote on the following pieces of legislation.

utterances.text: Resolution 626, sponsored by Councilmember Farrah Lewis, would call upon the United States Senate to pass and the President to sign

utterances.text: S-4814 to require the Secretary of Homeland Security to designate Haiti for temporary protected status.

utterances.text: Resolution 89A, sponsored by Councilmember Jennifer Gutierrez, would call on the New York State Assembly to pass and the Governor to sign legislation requiring each SUNY

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: The following bills are all sponsored by Deputy Speaker Dr.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Nantasha Williams.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Introduction 1127-C would amend and repeal sections of the New York City Charter and Administrative Code of the City of New York to change

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: certain and eliminate certain reporting requirements and change the dates of when specific reports are sent to the Council.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Introduction 1128A would establish a default reporting due date system for agency reports due to the Council for reports that don't have a specified deadline in law.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: And then lastly, Introduction 1129A would establish a procedure to be prescribed by the Speaker of the Council for how a city agency is to transmit reports and completion of operational milestones to the Council.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Introduction 1023, sponsored by Deputy Leader Chris Banks, would give property owners that need to register their property with HPD the option of doing so through an electronic registration system.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Thank you to Billy Eck, Tyler Isaiah Walls, Austin Malone, Jose Conde, and Dirk Spencer.

chapters.summary: Speaker Menin previews Intro 717-A by Council Member Yusef Salaam, requiring DOB to notify property owners with open permits about sign-off requirements.
chapters.title: Speaker Menin previews Intro 717-A on DOB permit sign-off notifications

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Introduction 717A, sponsored by Councilmember Yusuf Salam, would require the DOB to notify property owners with open permits that the permits must receive DOB sign-off.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: DOB would be required to email an initial notice within seven days of the issuance of a permit.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: The notice would inform property owners of the consequences of failing to obtain sign-off and provide instructions for accessing DOB's online self-service portal.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: DOB would also be required to send follow-up notifications if such permit has not been renewed and yet to receive sign-off within 30 days of expiration.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Thank you to Austin Malone, Margaret Lieford, Billy Eck, Jose Conde, and Dirk Spencer.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Introduction 259A, sponsored by Councilmember Shekhar Krishnan, would require the Department of Health and Mental Hygiene to collaborate with the DOE to develop materials for students and parents on the importance of dental care and fluoride.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Introduction 200A, sponsored by Councilmember Jennifer Gutierrez, would require the DOHMH

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Commissioner to develop materials to inform the public about options for obtaining doula care,

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: including information about state laws regarding access via doula to hospital spaces and Medicaid reimbursement for doula services.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: The bill would also require the development of a submission form to receive feedback from doulas working in city hospitals and would establish a doula advisory council.

chapters.summary: Speaker Menin previews Intro 211-A by Council Member Shahana Hanif, requiring DOHMH to conduct public education on fertility treatment services and insurance coverage.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Introduction 211A, sponsored by Councilmember Hanif, would require the Department of Health and Mental Hygiene to conduct a public education and outreach program on fertility treatment services.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Including information on insurance coverage and city-offered benefits.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Thank you to Christopher Pepe, Elizabeth Arts, and Joshua Newman.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu

chapters.summary: Council Member Chris Banks thanks Speaker Menin, the Housing Committee, and advocates, explaining that Intro 1023 allows property owners to complete HPD registration and pay fees online.
chapters.title: Council Member Banks advocates for Intro 1023 on HPD electronic registration

utterances.speaker: Chris Banks
utterances.text: Thank you, Majority Leader.

utterances.speaker: Chris Banks
utterances.text: I want to first of all, my start.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Quiet in the chambers, please.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: What's going on?

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: You may begin.

utterances.speaker: Chris Banks
utterances.text: Can I get my minute back?

utterances.speaker: Chris Banks
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Chris Banks
utterances.text: Appreciate it.

utterances.speaker: Chris Banks
utterances.text: Thank you, Majority Leader.

utterances.speaker: Chris Banks
utterances.text: I want to first of all start by thanking Speaker Menon for her leadership and for helping me bring this bill 1023 onto the floor.

utterances.speaker: Chris Banks
utterances.text: Thank you also, Chair Perina Sanchez and the Housing and Buildings Committee and staff and all the colleagues who signed on to the bill.

utterances.speaker: Chris Banks
utterances.text: Proud that the bill was able to get 46 members on the council who came together to support and sponsor this bill.

utterances.speaker: Chris Banks
utterances.text: Also, I want to thank the advocates and the property owners who kept raising this issue, especially the small property owners of New York's phone.

utterances.speaker: Chris Banks
utterances.text: You brought us a problem that you were dealing with year after year, and we helped get it fixed.

utterances.speaker: Chris Banks
utterances.text: Or Sponey, one member in multiple conversations, we've had conversations about the issues that were facing small property owners and

utterances.speaker: Chris Banks
utterances.text: the city, you know, with this particular bill dealing with this $13 fee that was being attached to this particular registration.

utterances.speaker: Chris Banks
utterances.text: And now the opportunity will allow us to pass this bill right now and you can fill out the building registration form online but you also still

utterances.speaker: Chris Banks
utterances.text: have to print it, you won't have to get it signed and send it to HPD by snail mail.

utterances.speaker: Chris Banks
utterances.text: And if you want to pay the fee online, that's a separate system.

utterances.speaker: Chris Banks
utterances.text: We call it an online registration, but you can't finish it online.

utterances.speaker: Chris Banks
utterances.text: So under this bill, owners will be able to fill out the form, sign it, pay the fee on one place on HPD's website, and the annual registration requirement stays in place.

utterances.speaker: Chris Banks
utterances.text: We're just making it easier for people to do what the city already asked them to do.

utterances.speaker: Chris Banks
utterances.text: For the small property owners in my district who answered their tenants'calls,

utterances.speaker: Chris Banks
utterances.text: and line up with peers and handle their own paperwork.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Thank you, Councilman.

utterances.speaker: Chris Banks
utterances.text: That's one of the last things that they would have to do now.

utterances.speaker: Chris Banks
utterances.text: I'm proud that we got this bill over the finish line, and thank you for all those folks who signed on.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Councilmember Hanif.

chapters.summary: Council Member Shahana Hanif speaks on the cost and complexity of fertility treatment and her bill requiring DOHMH to launch a multilingual public education campaign.
chapters.title: Council Member Hanif urges support for Intro 211 on fertility education

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: For New Yorkers hoping to start or grow their families, fertility treatment can be expensive, physically painful, and emotionally overwhelming.

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: Navigating insurance coverage only adds to that burden.

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: Too many New Yorkers are unaware that they may already qualify for fertility treatment coverage or financial assistance, thanks to protections and programs established by our partners in Albany.

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: Many of us appreciated Rep AOC's Instagram stories about her IVF journey because she made information about fertility care accessible and easy to understand.

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: But New Yorkers need more than AOC's personal Instagram to have the information they need when navigating their reproductive health care options.

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: Today we are voting on Intro 211, my fertility education bill, to help close that information gap.

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: This legislation requires the Department of Health and Mental Hygiene to launch a multilingual, citywide public education campaign

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: about fertility treatment options, including IVF and fertility preservation, insurance coverage requirements, Medicaid benefits, and available financial assistance.

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: The campaign will reach New Yorkers through public transit, link NYC kiosks, health care facilities, and annual outreach.

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: Despite growing awareness, misconceptions about fertility care persist, particularly in low-income communities.

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: Fertility care is too often left out of broader conversations about reproductive health and family planning, despite being an essential component of reproductive freedom.

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: Intro 211 will improve public understanding of fertility treatment and coverage, helping New Yorkers make informed decisions about the reproductive health care.

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: New York City must remain a bastion of reproductive freedom, including the freedom to pursue building a family.

utterances.speaker: Shahana K. Hanif
utterances.text: Colleagues, I urge you to vote yes on Intro 211.

chapters.summary: Council Member Jennifer Gutiérrez speaks on doula access, maternal health disparities, and her bill creating a doula bill of rights and advisory council; she votes aye.
chapters.title: Council Member Gutiérrez explains vote on doula bill Intro 200-A

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Permission to explain my vote?

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Permission, Grants.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: I've spoken to this body many, many times about the importance of doula services and increasing access, and as someone who had the privilege of having a doula with me during

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: both of my deliveries, I dream of one day making my really positive experience into the standard for everyone.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: And more and more New Yorkers are using doulas for their invaluable services.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Having a doula lowers preterm birth, lowers C-sections, and increases positive birth experiences.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: And doulas also have state-protected rights, but they are just not enforced or respected.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: They're often kicked out of hospital rooms and mistreated.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: And this can have an extremely negative emotional and physical outcome for their birthing client.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: And black women are the most mistreated in hospital settings, having a higher maternal mortality rate than white women.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: So protecting their access to doulas is crucial in keeping them safe.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Intro 200 creates a clear and public-facing materials that state that the laws birthing people have on accessing a doula in a hospital,

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: including information about Medicaid reimbursements, as well as an online feedback form for doulas to share their experiences working in these spaces.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: I've met with many, many, many doulas who are in this profession to support women, to support birthing people, but oftentimes their practice and their experience is not respected.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: This bill also calls for a doula advisory council to study their services in the city to help advise the citywide doula program of which this council helped codify and report on their findings.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: This bill addresses the systemic gaps in how New York City supports doulas by creating a clear doula bill of rights.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: We strengthen doula, by creating this clear doula bill of rights, we strengthen doula protections, and by strengthening doula protections, we strengthen birth outcomes across the city and advance a more equitable maternal health system.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: A doula just a few hours ago reminded me that doulas help families and uplift families.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: I also want to just thank my former chief of staff, Anya Lear, Madeline McGillivray, and our ledge of staff, Chris Pepe, for their support in this bill.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: And I vote aye.

chapters.summary: Council Member Kayla Santosuosso speaks on Resolution 447 for insurance coverage of PGTA testing and Resolution 637 for lactation consultation coverage.
chapters.title: Council Member Santosuosso advocates for PGTA and lactation coverage

utterances.speaker: Kayla Santosuosso
utterances.text: Thank you, Majority Leader.

utterances.speaker: Kayla Santosuosso
utterances.text: Today we are voting on two resolutions, Resolution 447 and Resolution 637, that would support new and future mothers and improve their access to critical health care services.

utterances.speaker: Kayla Santosuosso
utterances.text: The first, Resolution 447, calls on the state legislature to make sure that PGTA testing is covered by insurance for city employees.

utterances.speaker: Kayla Santosuosso
utterances.text: PGTA testing is an essential screening tool that can reduce the rate of miscarriage and reduce the time to pregnancy for those trying to conceive during the process of IVF.

utterances.speaker: Kayla Santosuosso
utterances.text: This kind of testing reduces the physical, emotional, and financial toll that IVF can have on would-be parents and increasing the rate of success and decreasing the chances of miscarriage.

utterances.speaker: Kayla Santosuosso
utterances.text: Despite all of this, insurance companies covering city employees still view PGTA testing as non-essential, forcing would-be parents to skip testing or pay costly fees out of pocket.

utterances.speaker: Kayla Santosuosso
utterances.text: This places unnecessary burdens on families and often increases the overall cost of IVF for everyone involved, including the insurance companies themselves.

utterances.speaker: Kayla Santosuosso
utterances.text: By requiring the insurance companies to cover these procedures, we can ensure that would-be parents can access this critical and life-changing health care.

utterances.speaker: Kayla Santosuosso
utterances.text: Thank you, Councilmember.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Your time is up.

utterances.speaker: Kayla Santosuosso
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Yep.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu

chapters.summary: Council Member Farah Louis discusses the Haiti crisis, the Flatbush building collapse, and calls for redesignation of Haiti for temporary protected status.
chapters.title: Council Member Louis urges support for Resolution 626 on Haiti TPS

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: This July, Mullen v.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Doe left thousands of Haitians vulnerable to deportation and without work authorization.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Our city is home to over 40,000 Haitians and families are being broken, especially in central Brooklyn.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: TPS is a lifeline for families who keep New York running.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: The Flatbush building collapse showed how its termination leaves our neighbors more vulnerable to unsafe housing exploitation and silence when disaster strikes.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Haiti continues to face armed conflict, gang violence, and displacement.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Sending people back into these conditions is immoral and unconscionable.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: No one should have to live in constant fear.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Today, we will advance Reso 626, calling to redesignate Haiti for TPS.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: I thank Chair Encarnacion and all of those who are signed on to this bill to help the most vulnerable New Yorkers, as our responsibility is to protect them.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: I urge my colleagues to vote yes.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Councilmember Aldebar, followed by Gutierrez.

chapters.summary: Council Member Shirley Aldebol recognizes the Albanian diaspora, thanks Council Member Farias, and urges support for Resolution 186.
chapters.title: Council Member Aldebol supports Resolution 186 on Albanian Independence Day

utterances.speaker: Shirley Aldebol
utterances.text: Thank you, Majority Leader.

utterances.speaker: Shirley Aldebol
utterances.text: Today, I am proud to support Resolution 186, recognizing November 28th as Albanian Independence Day in the City of New York.

utterances.speaker: Shirley Aldebol
utterances.text: The resolution reminds our Albanian diaspora that the City of New York not only recognizes their hard work and immense contributions, but will continue to commemorate all the diverse backgrounds that make New York City so special.

utterances.speaker: Shirley Aldebol
utterances.text: I would like to recognize the work of my colleague, Councilmember Amanda Farias, to make this resolution happen.

utterances.speaker: Shirley Aldebol
utterances.text: I urge you all to join us in support of this resolution, showing solidarity with the large Albanian community in the Bronx and in my District 13.

utterances.speaker: Shirley Aldebol
utterances.text: I, along with my colleagues, will be celebrating this occasion at City Hall on Monday, November 23rd, affirming that every New Yorker's story belongs here in the People's House.

utterances.speaker: Shirley Aldebol
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Council Member Jennifer Gutiérrez discusses barriers to emergency contraception for students and calls on SUNY and CUNY to install vending machines.
chapters.title: Council Member Gutiérrez urges support for Resolution 89A on emergency contraception

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: I just want to speak a little bit on Reso 89A, which calls on the state to require each SUNY and CUNY institution to install at least one vending machine that makes emergency contraception available for purchase.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Students across New York face significant barriers to accessing emergency contraception, including limited clinic hours, inconsistent campus policies, and uneven availability at pharmacies.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Young adults, particularly black, Hispanic, and uninsured students who make up a large share of SUNY and CUNY enrollment, are at a higher risk for unintended pregnancy and more likely to need contraceptive services.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Improving on-campus access supports students' health, autonomy, and ability to remain enrolled and succeed academically.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: I also just want to shout out the Coalition New York Birth Control Access Project that has been working with our state reps to pass this bill.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: And, of course, my co-sponsors, including my neighbor, Councilmember Dinowitz, who's been so supportive.

utterances.speaker: Jennifer Gutiérrez
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu

chapters.summary: Council Member Alexa Avilés discusses Puerto Rico's colonial status, the Financial Oversight and Management Board, and opposition to Project Esencia luxury resort.
chapters.title: Council Member Avilés speaks on Puerto Rico and Project Esencia

utterances.speaker: Alexa Avilés
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Alexa Avilés
utterances.text: Rolling blackouts, water shortages for days on end, and a government that tells Puerto Ricans to pay more and expect less.

utterances.speaker: Alexa Avilés
utterances.text: None of these crises are new.

utterances.speaker: Alexa Avilés
utterances.text: Puerto Rico is the world's oldest colony, and its political and economic system has long been controlled and exploited by the U.S.

utterances.speaker: Alexa Avilés
utterances.text: Government and its Wall Street allies.

utterances.speaker: Alexa Avilés
utterances.text: The pain of the island's colonial status isn't hypothetical.

utterances.speaker: Alexa Avilés
utterances.text: Take, for instance, for a decade, Puerto Rico has been governed by the Financial Oversight Management Board, also known as La Junta.

utterances.speaker: Alexa Avilés
utterances.text: This unelected body has ushered in a decade of austerity, cutting the public university system by 50%, closing public schools, rolling back worker protections, and freezing wages.

utterances.speaker: Alexa Avilés
utterances.text: Not one ounce of evidence of economic growth.

utterances.speaker: Alexa Avilés
utterances.text: Meanwhile, the people of Cabo Rojo say no to Project Esencia.

utterances.speaker: Alexa Avilés
utterances.text: Project Esencia, a $2 billion luxury resort proposed in Cabo Rojo, twice the size of Central Park, is given tax ascents.

utterances.speaker: Alexa Avilés
utterances.text: and will lead to massive displacement of Puerto Ricans.

utterances.speaker: Alexa Avilés
utterances.text: Puerto Rico no se vende, Puerto Rico se defiende, esencia no.

utterances.speaker: Alexa Avilés
utterances.text: Gracias.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Thank you, Councilmember.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Councilman Marano, followed by Hudson, and then Caban.

chapters.summary: Council Member Frank Morano speaks on the cost of IVF, proposes refundable tax credits for up to three cycles, and notes bipartisan support.
chapters.title: Council Member Morano urges IVF tax credit in Resolution 108A

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Thank you, Majority Leader.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: There are plenty of things in life I understand being reserved for wealthy people, private jets, yachts, and apparently decent tickets to a Knicks game, especially after they've won the championship.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: But the opportunity to become a parent shouldn't be one of them.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: I've spoken with friends, relatives, and many constituents who've exhausted their savings just for the chance to have a child.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: And as the father of two young children, I want more people to experience the joy of parenthood.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: And that's what my resolution, Reso 108, is all about.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: It urges Albany to create refundable tax credits covering 75% of eligible IVF expenses for up to three cycles not covered by insurance.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: I'm particularly proud of the bipartisan support this has received.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: In my view, the desire to build a family transcends politics, but we still need Albany to act, and I'm looking forward to making this a reality come January when the legislature is back.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Shaun Abreu
utterances.text: Councilmember Hudson, follow like a long.

chapters.summary: Council Member Crystal Hudson speaks on Lil' Kim's impact on hip-hop and Brooklyn, introducing a resolution designating July 11 as Lil' Kim Day.
chapters.title: Council Member Hudson introduces resolution honoring Lil' Kim

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: Today I'm introducing legislation to recognize someone whose name is synonymous with Brooklyn hip-hop, Lil'Kim.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: Born and raised in Brooklyn, Lil' Kim came into a rap industry where women were often expected to fit.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: into a very narrow box.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: She challenged that expectation from the very beginning.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: She took a genre that had long celebrated the sexuality and bravado of men and made room for women to express that same confidence on their own terms.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: As we approach the 30th anniversary of her debut studio album, Hardcore, it is worth remembering just how groundbreaking that album was for the culture at large.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: Her influence can be heard and seen in generations of artists who followed, from the way women approach their lyrics and their image to the freedom they have to define themselves as artists.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: And that influence is deeply rooted here in New York City.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: Lil'Kim is part of the legacy of Brooklyn and of hip-hop, a product of the culture, creativity, and talent that has made this city such an important force in music around the world.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: Her story is part of our city's history, and designating her birthday, July 11th, as Little Kim Day is an important opportunity to recognize her incredible career, and I'm proud to introduce this resolution today.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: First of all, I want to thank mi hermana boricua, Councilmember Aviles, for the resolutions we're going to be voting on today, and I hope my colleagues will support it.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: You know, there are now twice as many Puerto Ricans in the diaspora than there are on the island of Puerto Rico, and that is not a mistake.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: It's not a choice that we have made.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: The fight that we are having to end the fiscal control board to allow for

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: Puerto Ricans to have some variety and determine their own future doesn't come from what an organizer that I spent time with, that we spent time with recently in Puerto Rico said, a nostalgia for Puerto Rico of the past.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: It has everything to do that colonization has ravaged the beautiful resources of our island, has made it impossible for our city, our people to stay there

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: and forced us to migrate to the United States just to be able to survive.

utterances.speaker: Tiffany L. Cabán
utterances.text: So please stand with the people of Puerto Rico and vote aye on the resolutions.

utterances.text: And again, thank you, Councilmember Aviles.
